What Happens in a Crash (4-Step Sequence)
Interruptible Crash-Alert Interface Design
nodes.rationale: A crash alert that can't be quickly cancelled by a conscious rider is a system that will eventually be ignored; the sealed abort button, buzzer and status LED make the countdown legible and interruptible, usable with a glove on.

nodes.label: Weatherproofing as a Precondition, Not a Feature
nodes.rationale: Weatherproofing isn't a feature, it's a precondition — a device that fails in the rain fails on exactly the kind of day a rider is most likely to need it.

nodes.label: Phone-Independent Alerting (No Phone in the Loop)
nodes.rationale: The ESP32-S3 runs the entire device independently, with no phone in the loop, so the alert path never depends on the rider's phone being present, charged, or intact.

nodes.label: Power Continuity Through the Transmission Spike
nodes.rationale: Transmitting over the mobile network draws a hard current spike the instant it fires; this stage exists so the moment of the alert is never the moment the device gives out.

nodes.label: No App, No Login, No Excess (Bystander Lookup Design)
nodes.rationale: The bystander lookup opens in any phone's camera or browser with no app, no login and no relationship to the rider required, showing only triage-critical fields so the rest of the record stays private.

nodes.label: On-Chip MLC Crash Classification
nodes.rationale: Crash detection runs on the IMU's own machine-learning core (MLC) rather than in ESP32 application code, for lower latency (no round trip through the main CPU/scheduler) and lower power (the ESP32 stays low-activity while the IMU watches motion continuously, waking the main processor only when a likely crash is flagged).

nodes.label: Phone-Independent Cellular Alerting
nodes.rationale: The alert path deliberately does not depend on a paired phone; an on-device cellular modem means the crash notification goes out even if the rider's phone is destroyed, dead, or simply not on them.

nodes.label: Multi-Constellation GNSS Positioning
nodes.rationale: Multi-constellation GNSS (GPS/GLONASS/Galileo/BeiDou) trades a small amount of extra power draw for a materially faster, more reliable fix under tree cover, between buildings, or in road cuts and overpasses common on motorcycle routes.

nodes.label: Local Black-Box Impact Logging
nodes.rationale: The seconds immediately before and after an impact are logged locally regardless of whether the cellular alert succeeds, so a recoverable record survives even if network conditions fail exactly when they're needed most.

nodes.label: PMIC Transmission-Spike Protection
nodes.rationale: The power management IC keeps the board's supply stable through the sharp current spike the instant the cellular modem keys up, so the exact moment the device needs to send its alert is never the moment it browns out.

nodes.label: Interruptible Crash-Alert Interface Design
nodes.rationale: A crash alert a conscious rider can't quickly cancel is a system people learn to distrust and eventually disable; the sealed abort button, audible buzzer and status LED make the countdown legible and interruptible, usable with a glove on, in the rain, by someone who may be disoriented.

nodes.label: Medical Information (Blood Type, Allergies, Conditions, Medications, Donor Status, Contacts)
Incident Records (Crash Time, Impact Force, Location)
Row-Level Access Control / Restricted Public Lookup Function
nodes.rationale: Data is stored in a database with row-level access controls, so the database itself enforces who can read which records; the public emergency lookup uses a dedicated, restricted function rather than open access to the full database.

nodes.label: Minimal Emergency-Triage View via QR Scan
Administrator Data Visibility Scope
nodes.rationale: Project administrators (the research team) can see device status, live location while a rider's dashboard is open, and whether a crash has been flagged, for monitoring and demonstration purposes — but do not have a separate view into medical details beyond what's needed to operate the dashboard.

nodes.label: Manual Account Deletion Process
nodes.rationale: Deletion of an account and all associated data is currently a manual process handled by the research team rather than a self-service button — a known limitation the project intends to address.
